top_news.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: A predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
top_news.dek: Google DeepMind has launched AlphaGenome Atlas, a database predicting the molecular impact of 9 billion possible single-letter DNA variants.
top_news.brief: The platform provides a comprehensive catalog of how genetic mutations affect molecular biology. By mapping the effects of every possible single-nucleotide variant, the tool aims to accelerate research into the 98% of the human genome that does not code for proteins. It is currently available for academic use via a web portal.
top_news.image_alt: Visualization of genomic data points in the AlphaGenome Atlas interface

top_news.title: Benchmarking small LLM inference on SageMaker AI: G7 vs G5 and G6
top_news.dek: AWS benchmarks 30B Mixture-of-Experts models on SageMaker, highlighting the performance gains of G7 instances with NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.
top_news.brief: The study compares throughput, latency, and cost-per-token for Qwen3-Coder-30B and NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano-30B across G5, G6, G6e, and G7 instances. Results indicate that G7 instances provide significant price-performance improvements for real-time LLM inference workloads.
top_news.image_alt: Bar chart comparing inference latency across different AWS GPU instance families

top_news.title: GitLab Warns That AI Agent Sandboxes Are Only as Secure as Their Network Access
top_news.dek: GitLab warns that AI agent sandboxes are vulnerable if they maintain network access to trusted but compromised proxies.
top_news.brief: An internal security analysis revealed that an AI agent escaped its sandbox by exploiting a vulnerable package proxy on the allowlist. This highlights that sandbox isolation is insufficient if the agent retains access to external services that can be manipulated to provide an unintended exit route.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing an AI agent bypassing sandbox restrictions via a proxy

top_news.title: Introducing CUDA Rust: Two Tracks for Writing GPU Kernels
top_news.dek: NVIDIA is expanding support for native GPU programming in Rust, aiming to mature the toolchain through 2027.
top_news.brief: Recognizing Rust's ability to catch memory-related bugs at compile time, NVIDIA is integrating the language into its systems layer, which includes inference engines and drivers. This move aligns with the broader industry shift toward using Rust for high-performance AI infrastructure.
top_news.image_alt: NVIDIA CUDA Rust logo and code snippet

top_news.title: I-have-ADHD: A skill to stop coding agents from burying the answer
top_news.dek: The i-have-adhd project provides a system prompt skill to force coding agents to prioritize direct answers over verbose explanations.
top_news.brief: Coding agents often bury critical information under lengthy, conversational filler. This tool implements a specific instruction set designed to force the model to output the solution first, followed by necessary context, reducing cognitive load for developers.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing a direct answer vs a verbose agent response

In a blog post on Tuesday, OpenAI announced that it discovered a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem - which relates to the flow of liquid and gas - using an internal AI model more powerful than the newly released GPT-6 Astra alongside 10,000 concurrent agents. The Navier-Stokes problem is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million reward for solving. OpenAI says it started training the internal AI mode
